clue.text: Telegram admitting dad's qualified

indicators.note: a thing admitting another lets it in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a cable is an old word for a telegram
pa is an informal word for dad, the 's a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A telegram arrives announcing that father has passed his exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone qualified for a job is competent and fit to do it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sharp chopper — ace cut

indicators.note: a piece that is cut is removed, so the ace letter is taken away

parts.note: a cleaver is a butcher's chopper
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A sharp chopper used by an expert to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in the sense of quick-witted means intelligent and bright.

clue.text: Pictures group mountain climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a group
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: Photographs of a party scaling a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates are full-page illustrations in a book, so pictures.

clue.text: It requires guts to perform these dives

definitions.text: It requires guts to perform these dives

parts.words: It requires guts to perform these dives
parts.note: guts means courage, but these failed dives make a swimmer land on the stomach, so they literally require the gut

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed for certain daring plunges.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful dive landing flat on the stomach is the one meant, and the stomach is literally the guts.

clue.text: Planet's core hot from top to bottom

definitions.note: Planet's reads as 'planet is', the 's being the link

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter moves to the bottom, so that letter goes to the end

parts.note: the heart is the core of something
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The centre of a planet is hot all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from top to bottom' moves the H of HEART to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The world we live on is the third planet from the sun.

clue.text: Denies match official's welcoming cup-ties on a regular basis

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them in, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: ref is short for referee, the match official; with the 's it gives REFS

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A referee at a cup match is said to deny something while letting in a stream of fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match official's' reads as possessive but gives the plural of the referee's short name; 'on a regular basis' picks the even letters of the hyphenated word, and 'welcoming' houses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute a claim is to deny it or argue it is false, a close synonym.

clue.text: Journalists are heading off with hotel employees?

indicators.note: with its heading off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: porters carry luggage in a hotel

explanation.surface: A question whether journalists are leaving with the hotel staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the A of ARE, giving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters write news stories, so they are journalists.

clue.text: Handled fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of touching something matches handled, and the matted woollen cloth is a fabric.

clue.text: Dog ultimately cocks leg, producing state of panic

parts.note: to tail someone is to dog or follow them

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: pin is informal for leg

explanation.surface: A dog lifting its leg causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an aircraft's spiralling dive, the word is used figuratively for a state of chaotic panic.

clue.text: Son trying bad language

parts.note: trying and wearing both mean tiresome

explanation.surface: A tiresome son uses foul words.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursing and using oaths is bad language.

clue.text: Message this writer sent back with trouble

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as 'this writer', meaning me
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: An author returns a note complaining of some difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter's way of saying me, and 'sent back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic note sent between computers is a message, so the two are synonyms in modern use.

clue.text: Pure evil's monstrous, monstrous

indicators.note: monstrous suggests something misshapen and deformed, so the letters are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone condemns pure evil as truly monstrous, repeating the word for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first 'monstrous' rearranges PURE EVILS; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive is hideous and disgusting, which is what monstrous means in its sense of shocking.

clue.text: All over Spain wife is after most suitable present

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it, so the wife letter follows the 'most suitable' word

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
'the very thing' means the most suitable one
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Across the country, a Spanish wife hunts for the perfect gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found all over is found in every place, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Partially backing Starmer as the leader

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political comment on whether supporters back Keir Starmer as their party's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Labour leader and prime minister, which makes 'backing' read like political support.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor was the country's ruler, so a leader in the sense of supreme head.

clue.text: London possibly is centre for ambitious moneyman?

parts.note: London is an example of a capital city, so 'possibly'

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: London is the place for an ambitious financier.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invests money for profit is a believer in private wealth, so a moneyman.

clue.text: Adult prepared tortellini — a popular pasta, perhaps?

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: food prepared in a kitchen is made up from its ingredients, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A grown-up cooks tortellini, a well-loved pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popular pasta' is an example of the device itself: both words begin with P. 'perhaps' marks it as one example among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the same opening sound in neighbouring words, as the two P words here do, is the literary figure named.

clue.text: Seclusion is, to a lion, wretched

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Being shut away is miserable for a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set apart from others is seclusion, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Country clubs in lush ground

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard, as is a sot
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
land is ground

explanation.surface: Golf clubs on green grassy terrain suggest a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lush' looks like an adjective for green land, but it is the noun meaning drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern nation of the United Kingdom is a country in its own right.

clue.text: Cloth from China and money from Saudi Arabia?

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a friend
the rial is the currency of Saudi Arabia

explanation.surface: Fabric imported from China, paid for with Saudi money.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang (London street slang) 'china' means mate, from 'china plate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric or textile in general is called cloth, a synonym.

clue.text: Supports trendy contest

parts.note: to champion a cause is to support it, so champions means supports
hip means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Someone backs a fashionable competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament held to find the best competitor is a contest, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tango is an energy drink

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Tango, the British fizzy brand, is an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British fizzy orange drink, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal tea infusion is a drink.

clue.text: Plan where camper might go

definitions.meaning: inside canvas shelter, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A purpose is a plan, and a camper sleeps inside a canvas shelter, so the phrase splits in two.

clue.text: Tense Independent editor gets married

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
I is the abbreviation for Independent, as in a politician without a party

explanation.surface: A nervous editor at The Independent newspaper is getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is a British newspaper, which makes the surface read as office news.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie the knot is to marry, so a couple who are wed are joined in that sense.

clue.text: A thin boat at sea circles island home

indicators.note: a ring that circles something surrounds it, so the island letter goes inside
at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A slender vessel on the ocean sails round an island it calls home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges A THIN BOAT and 'circles' places I within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling place where someone lives is their home, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Family affair

definitions.meaning: a matter or topic of concern

explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's family, and a matter under debate is an affair.

clue.text: Heard of search for religious follower

indicators.note: heard means as spoken, so the word sounds like the one wanted

parts.note: to seek is to search

explanation.surface: Someone has heard of a search for a devout believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab is a religious follower.

clue.text: Criminal tries alibi, lacking right skills

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
lacking means the letters are without one piece, which is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A crook offers an alibi that lacks credibility, displaying certain talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges TRIES ALIBI and 'lacking right' drops one R from the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilities are talents or capacities to do things, the same as skills.

clue.text: Rodent entering that is foaming at the mouth

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the rodent goes into the other piece

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat creeps in, frothing at the mouth with rabies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foaming at the mouth' suggests a rabid animal but here means furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone foaming at the mouth is wildly angry, an idiom for being furious.

clue.text: Tramp returning with incomplete clue? One's supposedly intelligent!

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to plod is to walk heavily, to tramp

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver dismisses a vague clue, mocking someone who is meant to be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns PLOD into DOLP; 'incomplete' cuts the T off HINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea mammals of this family are widely regarded as among the cleverest animals, so the definition describes one by reputation.

clue.text: Beg chaps to leave maiden gift

indicators.note: one piece told to leave the other departs from it, so its letter is removed

parts.note: chaps are men
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden, an over with no runs scored
a treat is a gift or special pleasure

explanation.surface: The men are pleading for a girl to be left a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' drops M from MEN, giving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat someone is to beg or plead with them earnestly.
